common.purpose: Resolve for the I42 admission work how pool inputs become assertable, how example sources are organized, and which harness proves each P13 outcome row.
fixed_constraints: Each of the four examples is a complete manifest-backed program with can.project.json, can.errors.json, src/, README, and declared-only assets and dependencies that builds from scratch, passes real assertions, and completes its documented flow end-to-end from a staged layout.

Account-search follows P13 exactly: ordinary records, four named callbacks, one open sql::pool via near capture, a static descriptor, and the eleven-row outcome table; partial fragments plus harness-side behavior do not qualify.

Assertion rows map onto non-elided inputs in order and every function requires them; http::request and sql::transaction are harness-elided while sql::pool is an ordinary assertable input no expression can produce, leaving pool functions unassertable.
Statuses, headers, and bodies are provable over staged HTTP, swapping only in the pinned browser; raw versus supplied evidence is labeled per result; live provider calls never support a verdict.

pool_assertion_inputs.background: Mandatory assertions cannot supply the near sql::pool inputs of the loader and callback functions, because the harness elides requests and transactions but leaves pools as ordinary values no syntax constructs.
facts: Supplying pools from the harness reuses the frozen token object with no type-specific runtime work, and rows must still when-supply every pool operation or the live boundary refuses them.
Elision changes no green fixture since none takes a pool input; per-body open and close is today's only pool pattern and keeps checking exactly as before.
Keeping pools out of signatures forces per-request lifecycles inside callbacks, contradicting capture and multiplying connection work by request count.

app_source_layout.background: Four small servers share one anatomy of records, models, renderers, callbacks, routes, boot, and main, differing mainly in query and interaction focus.
facts: Single-file sources concentrate each program for linear review and remove provides and uses bookkeeping entirely.
Multiple src/ modules mirror genuine project layout and put cross-file checking, overlays, and definition jumps under admission coverage.
Both organizations clear the same completion bar of fresh build, real assertions, and documented runs; only review texture and realism differ.

negative_allocation.background: The eleven outcome rows divide into wire-visible facts and engine-visible swap decisions that demand different harnesses for direct proof.
facts: Raw HTTP staging asserts codes, headers, payloads, repeated parameters, and body limits quickly and repeatably for all trigger rows.
Browser runs assert fragment insertion on 200 and 422 plus its absence on 404, 405, 500, and 503 inside the pinned engine, row by row.
Localhost request policing and structured per-check output already exist in the I34 scenarios and extend to new ones unchanged.

pool_assertion_inputs.instructions: Select the assertability approach for captured pools, grounding the call in common and topics.pool_assertion_inputs.

criteria.elide_pool: Elide sql::pool inputs so the harness provides them: unassertable signatures become testable, historic results are untouched, and unprovisioned live use is still refused.
criteria.per_request_open: Keep pools out of signatures with per-request open and close: no checker edit, but capture is dropped and each request repeats connection setup.
criteria.review_needed: This evidence separates neither approach, or no approach holds the contracts.

app_source_layout.instructions: Select the source organization per example, grounding the call in common and topics.app_source_layout.

criteria.single_file: Concentrate each example in one src/main.can: linear review with no module bookkeeping and no multi-file demonstration.
criteria.multi_module: Decompose into src/ modules: authentic project shape with resolution and navigation coverage, plus linkage to keep coherent.
criteria.review_needed: This evidence separates neither organization, or none holds the contracts.

negative_allocation.instructions: Select the harness split for outcome rows, grounding the call in common and topics.negative_allocation.

criteria.split_by_observability: Match rows to harnesses by visibility: wire facts over staged HTTP, swap facts in the browser, one native witness per row.
criteria.http_first: Cover the full table over staged HTTP and use the browser for happy paths only: cheap deterministic rows with engine swap gaps on errors.
criteria.review_needed: This evidence separates neither split, or no split holds the contracts.
